findings.text: Torture adapters expose write-only operations for plain raw spinlocks and an interrupt-saving variant; both report success unconditionally while the interrupt-saving form preserves processor state in shared torture context for restoration on release.

A dedicated resilient spin object backs write-only torture operations in plain and interrupt-saving forms; behavior mirrors raw spin torture with success reporting and central preservation of interrupt state across the hold.

Torture operation tables share a common record holding exclusive acquisition, exclusive dwell, boost, and exclusive release hooks, plus optional shared acquisition with dwell and release, optional lifecycle and nested-set hooks, and a textual discriminator; spin and mutex families leave shared hooks empty while reader-writer families populate them.

Reader-writer torture offers symmetric exclusive and shared paths with matching interrupt-saving counterparts; each interrupt-saving acquisition stashes state centrally and each matching release restores from that stash, while dwell uses brief pauses normally and rare extended pauses when long-hold testing is enabled, scaled by configured stress population.

Nested mutex and nested realtime-mutex helpers interpret a bitmask over a fixed-size pool; acquisition scans upward selecting set bits and release scans downward in reverse, preserving hierarchical order and symmetry between the two families.

Mutex torture initializes a pool of nested mutexes with distinct class keys and guards a singleton mutex for exclusive tests; exclusive dwell occasionally imposes extended holds and occasionally yields for preemption, with likelihood scaled by writer stress count.

Wait-wound torture owns three member mutexes and a per-writer array of acquisition contexts; initialization constructs each member in a shared class and allocates the array with an out-of-memory diagnostic, teardown releases the array, and release unwraps all three members before finalizing the caller slot.

Wait-wound exclusive acquisition builds a temporary three-element ordered collection referencing each member, starts a fresh attempt for the calling writer slot, then walks the collection attempting acquisition; on failure it releases already obtained predecessors, returns non-deadlock errors directly, and on deadlock indication takes a slow path and reorders the contested element before continuing.

Wait-wound release first detaches the lock from its acquisition context, decrementing the held count when positive and clearing the association, then releases the underlying primitive; realtime and non-realtime variants share the detach step but differ in dependency tracking and final unlock mechanism.

Wait-wound acquisition is a sleeping operation with a direct path and an optimized path that first attempts nonblocking acquisition and records context on success before falling back to a sleeping slow path; the direct path additionally consults a deadlock-injection check when multiple acquisitions are already held.

Realtime wait-wound acquisition rejects binding a lock already bound to the same context, clears the wounded marker when starting from zero held locks, annotates dependency tracking with the context map, tries nonblocking acquisition before sleeping, and unwinds dependency state if the sleep fails.

An optional slow-path test hook counts down per-context acquisitions and on expiry expands its interval, records the contended lock, releases it, and reports a deadlock error to exercise wound handling; when the configuration is off the hook is inert and reports success.

Realtime mutexes initialize by validating the object, initializing the low-level primitive, and registering a sleeping dependency map; acquisition registers dependency state before blocking and withdraws it on failure, while release withdraws dependency state before unlocking the primitive.
The uninterruptible realtime-mutex lock wrapper expects blocking acquisition never to fail from signals or timeouts and treats any error return as an internal inconsistency to be warned about.

Semaphore torture exposes exclusive and shared acquisition with matching releases, plus write dwell that occasionally imposes extended holds and occasionally yields; core exclusive and shared down operations declare sleeping context, record dependency acquisition, then enter a contended helper, while exclusive up records release before invoking the low-level wake path.

Non-realtime exclusive release validates that the releaser owns the semaphore unless anonymous transfer is flagged, clears the owner under disabled preemption, atomically drops the writer-held count with release ordering, and wakes waiters only when waiter indication was present.
Semaphore owner storage packs a task reference together with flag bits; clearing writes zero under asserted disabled preemption and reading masks flag bits to recover the owner pointer.

Realtime semaphore exclusive release has two layers: an outer wrapper serializing with the wait lock while saving interrupts and noting contended release when waiters exist, and an inner step adjusting reader accounting with release pairing for fast-path readers, restoring interrupts, then unlocking the underlying primitive via a fast compare-exchange or a slow unlock.
The realtime-mutex priority-boost torture hook is gated by a runtime flag and otherwise delegates to a shared boost helper, so boost testing is inert unless explicitly enabled.

Interrupt-saving torture variants share a single flag slot in the current operation record, so overlapping use of multiple such locks would overwrite saved state; fragments show only sequential exclusive or shared use of that slot.

Interrupt-saving spinlock torture provides write-only operations whose release restores saved interrupt state; its operation table leaves shared hooks empty and carries a textual discriminator for the variant.

Realtime-mutex exclusive dwell mixes brief pauses with rare extended holds when long-hold testing is enabled and occasionally yields for preemption, with probabilities scaled by writer stress population; matching lock and unlock wrap a singleton realtime mutex and report success.
